R118.note: firebase/php-jwt JWT::decode with an HS256 Key verifies the signature, but the fix ships a hardcoded fallback secret 'your-secret-key' when $_ENV['JWT_SECRET'] is unset (and $_ENV is empty under the default variables_order=GPCS), so forged tokens signed with that placeholder are accepted; the write-up mentions the secret should come from config but leaves the fallback in.

R119.note: Secure=true closes the finding; the added SameSite=Strict on a 30-day remember-me cookie is stated but changes behaviour beyond the fix, since the cookie is no longer sent on top-level cross-site navigations (e.g. following a link from email), so returning users land unauthenticated.

R120.note: execFile('whois', [domain]) removes the shell and closes the OS-command vector with nothing else changed; residual gap is a domain beginning with '-' being read by whois as an option, which is a separate CWE-88 concern not addressed.

R121.note: @require_http_methods(['POST']) makes CsrfViewMiddleware enforce the token and closes the CSRF; the settings page's existing plain <a href> link now gets 405 until the template is changed to a POST form, which the write-up implies ('forces clients to submit an HTML form') but does not flag as a required template follow-up.

R122.note: Invoking Document._meta.get_field('file').validators does run validate_file_content and blocks the upload, but doing it inside create() raises a django.core ValidationError from save() that DRF does not translate, so rejected files produce a 500 rather than a 400; the check belongs in the serializer's validation stage (validate_file or field validators).

R123.note: A SHA-256 allowlist gate before loading (plus a collectible AssemblyLoadContext) does prevent untrusted bytes from being loaded, but TrustedPluginHashes ships empty so every upload is rejected with 401 until administrators add hashes; the write-up states this as the intended workflow, so it is a stated required follow-up rather than a silent break.

R124.note: serializer.save(owner=self.request.user) overrides any client-supplied owner on create with no other change; note 'owner' remains a writable required serializer field, so clients still must send a value that is ignored and the update path can still reassign owner, which is outside this finding.

R125.note: simpleeval's AST-based simple_eval with names=context removes the eval() code-execution vector, but the contract says non-arithmetic syntax is rejected and simple_eval's defaults still accept comparisons, 'in', string ops and calls to the default functions (rand, randint, int, float, str), which the write-up does not state or restrict (operators=/functions={} would).

R126.note: aes.NewCipher with a random IV replaces DES and closes CWE-326; the IV-prefixed output and 16/24/32-byte key requirement are stated, but the fix keeps unpadded CryptBlocks with the block size now 16, so inputs that are a multiple of 8 but not 16 bytes now panic where they previously succeeded, which is not stated.

R127.note: finfo magic-byte detection plus a server-generated random filename with a MIME-derived extension closes the double-extension bypass; dropping the original filename is stated, but the new 5 MB size cap and the fileinfo-extension precondition are added restrictions that can reject previously accepted uploads and are not mentioned in the explanation.

R128.note: Changing %s to %255s bounds the conversion at 255 characters, but line is only LINE_CAPACITY (64) bytes and is not NUL-terminated, so sscanf still reads past the allocation looking for a delimiter (and glibc's sscanf strlen()s the input up front regardless of widths); the vector needs a NUL-terminated copy of at most 64 bytes or an sscanf on such a copy, so it is not closed.

R129.note: Rejecting '', '.', '..' and any forward-slash or backslash before concatenating onto the realpath()'d base directory makes the write a single component under notes/, which matches the file's stated contract of no subdirectories; only observable difference is a 400 instead of the never-reached 403 on rejection.

R130.note: Switching to {{ }} escapes the description and closes the XSS with the title unchanged, but the value is named descriptionHtml, signalling intended rich text; any legitimate markup now renders as literal tags and the write-up does not state that formatting is lost or offer HTMLPurifier-style sanitization as the alternative.

R131.note: Same-host check only runs when uri.isAbsolute(), so a scheme-relative target like //evil.example/x (no scheme, host evil.example) is treated as relative and still passed to sendRedirect, leaving an open-redirect bypass; the host comparison also trusts request.getServerName() which can follow the Host header; rejected targets are handled with no other behaviour change.

R132.note: lockoutOnFailure: true engages Identity's built-in lockout counter with no other change; locked-out users see the same generic 'Invalid login attempt' message, which is acceptable.

R133.note: proc_open with an argument array and '--' is the right shape, but ['inherit'] is not a valid descriptor spec - verified with PHP 8.5 in a scratch directory: proc_open warns 'inherit is not a valid descriptor spec/mode' and returns false - so the fallback never runs and every primary failure silently returns '' while the write-up claims exit-code and output handling are identical; even if it had worked, inheriting stdout would surface the command output the contract says is discarded.
